plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large daisy-like flower heads composed of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disk. Heads track the sun when young and are widely grown for seed, oil, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, the United States, and Argentina
plants.funFact: The sunflower head is actually made of hundreds to thousands of tiny individual flowers arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: A low evergreen shrub forming dense carpets on moorlands, covered in tiny bell-shaped flowers. It thrives in acidic, nutrient-poor soils and is a vital nectar source for bees in late summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Moorlands and heathlands of Scotland, northern England, Ireland, Scandinavia, and other parts of northern and western Europe
plants.funFact: Heather honey is prized for its jelly-like texture and strong flavor, and the plant was historically used for thatching, bedding, and brewing ale.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower bearing dense plumes of tiny golden flower heads. It spreads by rhizomes to form large stands in meadows, roadsides, and open fields, and attracts many pollinators in late summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to fall (July to October)
plants.location: Native to eastern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and insect-carried; the real culprit is usually ragweed blooming at the same time.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with large, crimson, dome-shaped flower heads surrounded by red bracts. It grows in sandy soils of sclerophyll forests and is the floral emblem of New South Wales.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (August to November)
plants.location: Sandstone areas around Sydney and the Blue Mountains, New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: Its name comes from the Greek 'telopos' meaning 'seen from afar,' and the flower heads are made of hundreds of tiny individual flowers that are pollinated by birds.
